The Harvard College Fund

A century of giving forward

Give Now
Harvard College Fund
  • HCF Staff Directory
  • Giving and Recognition
  • Associates

One hundred years ago, 33 Harvard College alumni launched a new effort to support students then, and for the future. Their collective generosity laid the foundation for the Harvard College Fund.

Hundreds of thousands of alumni, parents, and friends have rallied behind the Harvard College Fund mission since then. This community helps the Harvard College Fund go to work right away: addressing urgent issues, building momentum for new ideas, and supporting everyone at the College (undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty) through every step of their Harvard journey.

As the Harvard College Fund celebrates a century of giving forward, we look toward the unlimited possibility of the next 100. Whether you’ve been part of this caring community for decades or are ready to show your support now, we invite you to be a part of it.

Join us for the next 100 and see what we can build together.

Why it matters

Contributions are immediately available.

Contributions to the Harvard College Fund are available to the College right away. Unlike endowment funds, which are often committed to specific purposes and distributed gradually over time, the Fund can be spent in the year it is given.

That means it can respond directly to what undergraduates need as those needs arise, rather than only to what a gift was earmarked for decades earlier.

70% of HCF gifts are under $1,000. Impact is built by many people giving something, not a few giving a lot.
22× the near-term impact of an endowment dollar, because HCF dollars are flexible and immediately usable.

What a century of giving has built.

Each of these is an area the Fund supports, not a line item any single gift paid for. Contributions arrive without a designated purpose, so the College directs them to where they are needed that year. That is what makes the list this long.

  • Classroom to TableA program that seats three to five undergraduates and their professor at a restaurant in Harvard Square, on the College’s tab. It turns a lecture course into a conversation that keeps going after the last class.→
  • Financial AidNeed-based aid that Fund-supported expansion has widened decade by decade. It is why every admitted student can graduate without debt, regardless of what their family can pay.→
  • General EducationThe four-course requirement that connects a discipline to the questions students carry beyond Harvard. It keeps what undergraduates study adapting as quickly as the world they graduate into.→
  • Hands-On LearningThe Fabrication Makerspace, the Active Learning Labs, field study at Harvard Forest and Reimagining Experiential Education. Together they put laser cutters, engineering benches and working woodland within reach of any student with an idea worth building.→
  • House LifeThe twelve residential Houses students join on Housing Day, each with its own faculty deans and resident tutors. The Fund sustains the intramurals, formals and common spaces that make a House the center of the next three years.→
  • LibrariesThe oldest library system in the United States, founded in 1638, and the largest academic library in the world. It runs from Widener’s stacks to Lamont’s all-night reading rooms, open at the hours students actually work.→
  • Pre-Orientation ProgramsSix programs that bring incoming students to campus before term starts: FOP in the outdoors, FUP in the city, FAP in the arts, FIP for international students, FYRE and LIFE. Most first-years meet their first Harvard group here, a week before their first class.→
  • Public ServiceService that begins the summer before first year and carries on past Commencement. The Fund supports the stipends, term-time programs and fellowships that make that work possible for students who could not otherwise give a summer away unpaid.→
  • ResearchWork reaching from natural and artificial intelligence to new ways of treating and preventing disease, at the university that debuted the country’s first programmable computer. The Fund supports the grants that let undergraduates take part in it.→
  • Senior Week EventsThe stretch between the last exam and Commencement, filled with events for the graduating class. It is the send-off: the last time the class gathers before a lifetime in the alumni community.→

Harvard College Fund Across the Decades

100 years of meeting the moment

1926

After 33 alumni volunteers come together to establish the Harvard Fund, the first appeal is sent to alumni. 3,260 individuals from over 600 cities give nearly $125,000, equivalent to $2.3 million today.

1942

Giving jumps 23 percent. These dollars support the University’s activities during World War II and later help launch the new General Education program, where students can connect what they learn at the College with the lives they’ll lead after graduation.

1970

Mather and Currier open, completing a system of 12 Houses that fully embed the educational experience into student residences. The HCF supports every aspect of House life and strengthens the spaces where students learn and thrive.

2004

The Harvard Financial Aid Initiative launches, expanding an industry-leading program started in 1934 and opening doors to exceptional students of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Today, the HCF helps ensure every student can graduate debt-free.

Video

2016

The Harvard Campaign for Arts and Sciences concludes after raising 278,000 individual gifts. 20,000+ volunteers across 84 classes worked together to raise over $850 million.

2018

FYRE (First-Year Retreat and Experience) joins five other pre-orientation programs, all supported by the HCF, to help new students prepare for life at the College.

2025

HCF donors step forward to help Dean Hopi Hoekstra ensure research continuity at the FAS. These gifts immediately sustain vital areas of the mission, including teaching, the undergraduate experience, and discoveries that benefit the world.

Voices from a century of giving

And we’re just getting started! Thanks to the collective impact of alumni, parents, and friends, the Harvard College Fund continues to create continuity amid uncertainty, support groundbreaking discoveries, and open doors to extraordinary students.

Whether you’ve been part of this caring community for decades or are ready to show your support now, you’re invited to be part of something legendary. Join us as we celebrate a century of giving forward.
